Rare Earth Mettle gets a very glitzy production but, while the shifting negotiations that make up the plot hold the attention, their results have to be imagined.
Indeed, Jewishness turns out to be entirely irrelevant to a baggy, shapeless but appealingly acted play that seems to have drawn attention for all the wrong reasons.
Ultimately though, Rare Earth Mettle is frustratingly hard to connect with and, in Pirie's uncompromisingly stark production, proves as dry as the salt flats on which it is mainly set.

Terrifically played by Arthur Darvill, Finn is the best thing about Hamish Pirie’s over-long production which overreaches for contemporary relevance by scooping up just about every hot topic in the news.

While questions are raised over the main satire at the heart of Rare Earth Mettle, I’m also left wondering what exactly the point is behind the actors engaging in elaborate dance numbers to electronic music in between scenes.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this controversy-shadowed satire about lithium mining and tech capitalism. While some praise its ambitious scope and entertainment value, many find it sprawling, heavy-handed, and dramatically flat despite timely themes.
